findings.how_to_check: Re-extract refs_fullname.dta from profile_names.dta into a temporary file and check row-by-row identity with the cached file. Identify a stable primary key such as histid or unique_ID and test uniqueness with isid in both datasets.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist a stable record identifier (such as histid or unique_ID) in refs_fullname.dta and merge on that key using assert(match) and isid, rather than relying on mutable row numbers (_id = _n).
findings.title: Cached profile reference names are merged by mutable row index rather than invariant record identifier
findings.what_the_code_does: The script creates a synthetic row index with gen long _id = _n on profile_names.dta and executes merge 1:1 _id using refs_fullname.dta, assert(match). It verifies that both datasets share identical row counts and that refs_fullname.dta is newer with matching version characteristic, but does not verify that corresponding rows represent the same census record.
findings.why_it_matters: If profile_names.dta is re-sorted, updated, or extracted without synchronously rebuilding refs_fullname.dta, reference names can be matched to the wrong census records without a merge assertion failure. While the one-decimal benchmark checks at lines 161-176 catch coarse divergence, small row shifts could corrupt the reported three-decimal Jaro-Winkler means without triggering the one-decimal exact-match check.

findings.how_to_check: In profile_names.dta, check for records where namefrst_ml!="" & strtrim(namefrst_ml)=="" or namelast_ml_ditto!="" & strtrim(namelast_ml_ditto)=="", and compare summary statistics under the exact raw equality condition vs strtrim.
findings.suggested_fix: Either align the fallback condition to the exact linkage pipeline logic (or test and confirm whether whitespace-only records exist), or soften the description in line 183 to state that Ours+Anc is a field-by-field empty-string fallback approximation to the linkage tables' New transcription.
findings.title: The 'Ours+Anc' fallback rule diverges from the linkage pipeline's New transcription definition
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 108-111 construct the fallback using strtrim(namefrst_ml)=="" and strtrim(namelast_ml_ditto)=="", substituting Ancestry field-by-field, and line 183 describes Ours+Anc as 'ours with Ancestry's name wherever the model field is empty, field by field, as the linkage tables' New transcription'. However, the linkage construction in 1_divide_and_clean_everyoneV5_women_addedV2.do:168-173 tests raw string emptiness (namefrst...=="" and namelast...=="") before abeclean, retaining whitespace-only strings rather than falling back to Ancestry, and also invalidates model transcriptions where filename-row duplicates exist (N>1 & _merge==3).
findings.why_it_matters: If whitespace-only model fields or duplicate filename-row pairs exist, the Ours+Anc series reported in profile_names_jw.md does not strictly reflect the New transcription fed to the linkage pipeline, despite the generated markdown text explicitly equating them.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to claims stated in the script comments and the generated markdown text.

External census and profile datasets (profile_names.dta, refs_fullname.dta) reside on external storage outside the repository and could not be inspected; runtime data characteristics were inferred from source code.
The Stata pipeline was not executed, so runtime execution and behavior of the external SSC jarowinkler package could not be verified directly.
The checked-in MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md file predates the addition of the Ours+Anc series, so the newly generated output values could not be compared against existing committed results.
summary: The Jaro-Winkler comparison script is defensively implemented with robust guards against empty-string agreement inflation, clear separation of comparison sources from ground truth, and comprehensive pre-output assertions that reproduce benchmark sample counts and exact-agreement shares. The most important remaining issue is that cached profile reference names are merged using a positional row index (_id = _n) rather than an invariant record identifier, creating a vulnerability if input sort orders shift. Additionally, the new 'Ours+Anc' fallback rule uses trimmed emptiness rather than the exact raw emptiness and duplicate handling of the linkage pipeline it references.
